verdict: Nasi ayam wins narrowly on calories. But nasi campur can be the best choice if you pick your dishes and vegetables wisely.
why: Nasi ayam is about 600 kcal, nasi campur with fried chicken and 2 vegetables about 650 kcal.
Protein is the same, about 28 g each. Fat is also almost the same, 23 g and 24 g.
Nasi campur has vegetables, so there's fibre to help you feel full. This is an advantage nasi ayam doesn't have.
But it's easy to overdo nasi campur: extra dishes, rice drowned in gravy, vegetables in santan (coconut milk). Calories can go up a lot.
when_a: Nasi ayam suits you when you want a fixed portion that's easy to estimate.
when_b: Nasi campur is great when you pick 1 protein dish and 2 stir-fried or boiled vegetables, with a little gravy.
tip: At a nasi campur stall, take vegetables first before the other dishes. Let vegetables fill half the plate, one scoop of rice, and just a little gravy.

faq.q: Which is better, sayur lemak or stir-fried vegetables?
faq.a: Stir-fried or boiled vegetables are usually lower in calories. Sayur lemak (vegetables in coconut milk) is okay, just take a little.

faq.q: Does curry gravy on rice have a lot of calories?
faq.a: Yes, the gravy has oil and santan. Ask for a little gravy or have it on the side, so you can control it.
